fish.name: Mist Nibbler
fish.flavor: It sips fog off the surface like tea gone cold. Politely declines to be impressive.

fish.name: Pinecone Perch
fish.flavor: Scaled like the forest floor's favorite litter. Squirrels have tried to bury it twice.

fish.name: Fog Minnow
fish.flavor: Barely there, even in the bucket. Netting one feels less like fishing and more like an accusation.

fish.name: Button Bream
fish.flavor: Round, shiny, and exactly the size of the button missing from your good coat. Coincidence, it insists.

fish.name: Sock Eel
fish.flavor: Warm, stripey, and always found alone. Somewhere out there is a drawer missing its partner.

fish.name: Teakettle Trout
fish.flavor: Whistles faintly when the water is about to boil with mayflies. Sensible folk set their mornings by it.

fish.name: Mumbling Bullhead
fish.flavor: It mutters into the mud all night long. Nobody has caught a full sentence, only complaints about the cold.

fish.name: Lantern Dace
fish.flavor: Carries a soft glow like a candle being walked carefully upstairs. Snuffs itself out of shyness when netted.

fish.name: Porridge Carp
fish.flavor: Thick, warm-colored, and dense enough to legally count as breakfast. Prefers its bait with a pinch of salt.

fish.name: Drizzle Darter
fish.flavor: Only bites when the rain is gentle. Downpours, in its opinion, are showing off.

fish.name: Freckled Yawner
fish.flavor: Yawns so wide it occasionally swallows the hook out of sheer boredom. You almost feel guilty. Almost.

fish.name: Moth-Wing Minnow
fish.flavor: Fins like dusty wings, forever drawn to lantern-light on the dock. It flutters more than it swims.

fish.name: Napping Loach
fish.flavor: Found dozing under sunken logs at every hour of the day. Being caught is the most exercise it gets all year.

fish.name: Cinnamon Sculpin
fish.flavor: Smells faintly of baked goods, which science cannot explain and grandmothers refuse to.

fish.name: Whisper Chub
fish.flavor: Hold it to your ear and it says nothing at all, but it says it very softly.

fish.name: Dewbell Roach
fish.flavor: Rings, very faintly, when lifted from the water at dawn. Nobody has ever found the bell.

fish.name: Hiccup Pike
fish.flavor: Strikes in startled little bursts, apologizing between each one. Its hiccups can be heard through the hull of a rowboat.

fish.name: Backwards Bass
fish.flavor: Swims tail-first and remembers things before they happen. It knew you would read this.

fish.name: Second-Moon Smelt
fish.flavor: Only rises on nights when the moon's reflection looks fuller than the moon. It prefers the copy.

fish.name: Millpond Ray
fish.flavor: Flat as a skipping stone and twice as smug about it. Glides under the docks all summer, collecting shade.

fish.name: Pewter Grinner
fish.flavor: Grins with the fixed cheer of an heirloom teapot. Polishing it is discouraged by everyone who has tried.

fish.name: Rumor Carp
fish.flavor: Grows an inch every time someone retells the story of catching it. The lake record is technically hearsay.

fish.name: Knotgrass Eel
fish.flavor: Ties itself into knots sailors haven't invented yet. Untangling one voids no warranties but tests every patience.

fish.name: Echo Bleak
fish.flavor: Repeats the last splash it heard, one beat late and slightly wrong. A school of them can ruin a quiet afternoon beautifully.

fish.name: Ferryman's Chub
fish.flavor: Will escort your boat across the lake for the price of one coin-sized scale. Refunds are unheard of and unwise to request.

fish.name: Toadstone Goby
fish.flavor: Folklore says the little stone in its head cures melancholy. The goby, for the record, is perfectly cheerful without it.

fish.name: Clockwise Koi
fish.flavor: Circles the same patch of water so precisely you could wind a watch by it. On the solstice, it pauses. Nobody knows what for.

fish.name: Widow's Lantern
fish.flavor: A cold blue light bobbing far from shore, precisely where a light should not be. Follow it with your line, never with your boat.

fish.name: Grandmother Pike
fish.flavor: Older than the mill, the dam, and the argument about the dam. Locals nod to the water before rowing over her spot.

fish.name: Inkwell Gar
fish.flavor: The water darkens wherever it swims, as though the lake were signing something. Nobody has read the terms.

fish.name: Stitchling Trout
fish.flavor: Seamed down each flank in tidy red thread, as though someone mended it and let it go. The stitching is always fresh.

fish.name: The Pale Procession
fish.flavor: Never caught alone: it arrives trailing seven paler copies of itself, each slightly less certain that it exists.

fish.name: Sunken Chapel Char
fish.flavor: Nests inside the flooded chapel's bell and hums low on foggy mornings. The bell, respectfully, hums back.

fish.name: The Long Quiet
fish.flavor: It passes beneath your boat for a full minute and a half. The frogs stop. The pines lean in. Then the lake exhales.

fish.name: Yesterday's Catch
fish.flavor: It is, verifiably, the exact fish you caught yesterday, down to the scar from your own hook. You did not catch a fish yesterday.

fish.name: The Hollow Saint
fish.flavor: A pale fish with soft light where its bones should be. Anglers who kneel to release it report cured sniffles and mysteriously organized tackle boxes.

fish.name: The Unstill Water
fish.flavor: A ripple that grew tired of being temporary. Reeling it in feels like arguing with the weather, and winning, barely.

fish.name: The Ferryman's Toll
fish.flavor: It surfaces only for those with nothing left to pay. Coins have been found in the bellies of fish that never met a coin. It keeps the ledger.

fish.name: The Moon's Understudy
fish.flavor: On nights the moon cannot make it, this rises from the lake bed and glows gamely in its place. The performance is imperfect, but the effort is beloved.

fish.name: The First Reflection
fish.flavor: Before anything ever looked into the lake, the lake looked into itself, and this is what looked back. For the moment you hold it, everything you have ever seen flickers across its scales — and then, gently, it lets you let it go.
